chapter: Barnet, 52nd Street and New York recording dates
title: More New York record dates: Sarah Vaughan, Buck Clayton, Eckstine
summary: He recorded with Tony Scott and Sarah Vaughan, with Buck Clayton for John Hammond, and in Eckstine's big band.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Also did a record date -- and I forgot the tune we did on it with Tony Scott, the clarinet player, and Sarah Vaughan was singing on this date. I don't know if we did "Chelsea Bridge." Ben Webster was on it also. But we did some good things. It's been so long, I forgot the particular tunes that we did on this thing. They were good.

And, of course, John Hammond used to have a lot of dates around there then because he used to use Buck Clayton on quite a few. He used Buck as the leader on quite a few things, and I played a few of those things with Buck, and they would really swing, you know, some of these things.

But almost every day you'd be recording with somebody. I know Eckstein came in town. He wanted to record, and he used a big band, with Eckstein -- a lot of us that never really played with him, we recorded with his band around, Dexter Gordon, myself, a bunch of us did.
But this is during the same period of time that we all worked 52nd Street. Musicians were available because they were right in town working, you know, was very easy to get them together.
